bib.title: Bandit Algorithms, Chapter 12: The Exp3-IX Algorithm

question: How can Exp3 be modified so the adversarial-bandit regret is small in expectation and also concentrated, giving a high-probability bound?
hypothesis: Biasing the importance-weighted loss estimator (implicit exploration) controls its variance at the price of some bias, yielding O(sqrt(nk log(k/delta))) regret with probability 1-delta.
contributions: Exp3-IX (Algorithm 10) with biased estimator Y_ti = I{A_t=i}Y_t/(P_ti+gamma)
Theorem 12.1: two high-probability regret bounds, one delta-free, one delta-tuned
Lemma 12.2: new concentration bound using negatively correlated estimators

limits: Chapter gives no explicit tight counterexample showing Exp3 has no high-probability bound; it only says the importance-weighted estimator variance is large (Fig 11.4 in previous chapter).
The delta-free and delta-tuned trade-off is deferred to Chapter 17.
Analysis uses a fixed horizon-dependent learning rate; anytime version only in Note 3 without proof.
Simulation settings for Figs 12.1 and 12.2 are only sketched in exercises (runs, seeds not given).
practices: Use eta=sqrt(2 log(k+1)/(nk)) and gamma=eta/2 for a single algorithm valid for all delta (Thm 12.1.1).
Use eta=sqrt((log k + log((k+1)/delta))/(nk)) and gamma=eta/2 when delta is fixed in advance for the better bound (Thm 12.1.2).
For an anytime algorithm use eta_t=sqrt(log(k)/(kt)), gamma_t=eta_t/2 (Note 3).
Exp3.P (mixing with the uniform distribution and biased estimates) is an alternative requiring delta (Note 6, Ex 12.3).
